result.title: TAP: Tapping the Discriminative Potential of Frozen Representations for Class-Incremental Learning
result.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures. Code is included as an ancillary file
result.summary: Pre-trained models provide transferable representations for class-incremental learning (CIL). However, sequentially adapting these representations introduces optimization costs and may disrupt old-class feature structure. This motivates us to explore whether the discriminative potential of these representations can be further exploited by continually accumulating class information while keeping the encoders frozen. To this end, we propose TAP, a new and novel framework for tapping the discriminative potential of frozen representations in class-incremental learning. It accumulates visual and semantic class information in the frozen CLIP embedding space with only lightweight optimization. TAP comprises three modules: class-conditional visual distribution modeling, class-adaptive semantic calibration, and visual-semantic posterior fusion. The first module retains class means and within-class scatters, combining class-specific and shared covariances to stabilize distribution estimation. The second module learns class-specific weights over text templates from current-task images, adapting text representations to downstream classes. The third module combines the visual and semantic posteriors through a weighted product of experts for prediction over all seen classes without retaining images from previous tasks. Across nine datasets under two incremental protocols, TAP achieves state-of-the-art performance, attaining the highest average incremental and final-stage accuracies among the compared methods. The code is provided as an ancillary file.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TAP 框架，在冻结的 CLIP 嵌入空间中用类别条件视觉分布建模、类自适应语义校准和视觉-语义后验融合累积类信息，仅做轻量优化以实现类增量学习。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线的推理机制距离较远，但其在冻结表征上建模类条件协方差并以专家乘积融合视觉与语义后验的做法，可能为「视觉细节在内部状态中保留多少、如何与语言先验结合」提供可核查的线索。
